name: Pinterest
verdict: Two reviews: Pinterest approves Trial access before you get an app ID, then a Standard access upgrade with an OAuth demo video is needed for production. About 1-3 weeks in total.
needGuide: Yes — request Trial access first, then record the OAuth demo video for the Standard upgrade.

auth.detail: Authorization code at https://www.pinterest.com/oauth/; token endpoint https://api.pinterest.com/v5/oauth/token with Basic auth. Access tokens last 30 days; only continuous refresh tokens are supported (60-day expiry, refreshable indefinitely; apps created before 2025-09-25 must send continuous_refresh=true). PKCE not documented. Sandbox host api-sandbox.pinterest.com.

effort.timeToProduction: about 1-3 weeks (Trial review plus Standard review; Pinterest says allow a few days before following up)

approval.gate: Two reviews. Trial access is reviewed by Pinterest before you get an app ID and secret; Trial apps have daily rate limits and Pins and Boards they create are visible only to the creator (sandbox). Standard access (higher per-minute limits, recommended for production) requires an Upgrade request with a demo video showing the OAuth flow, an API action and that no sensitive data is stored; Pinterest asks even for a single-user app.

scopes.why: Read and write scopes per resource (boards, pins, ads); new apps can get 403s on boards or Pins without user authorization.
scopes.summary: Examples: boards:read (and boards:read_secret), pins:write (and pins:write_secret), ads:read. Apps registered on or after 2026-09-14 may get 403 PINNER_DATA_ACCESS_DENIED when requesting boards or Pins without user authorization. Scope-specific review gates were not documented beyond the Standard upgrade.

prerequisites: Account and owner: A Pinterest business account administers the app, with a verified email and accepted Developer Terms of Service under My apps. Use a company-owned business account.

Where you register: Pinterest business account -> developers.pinterest.com -> My apps -> Connect app -> request Trial access; later Manage -> Configure -> Redirect URIs; My apps -> Upgrade for Standard access

registerAt.path: Pinterest business account -> developers.pinterest.com -> My apps -> Connect app -> request Trial access; later Manage -> Configure -> Redirect URIs; My apps -> Upgrade for Standard access

steps.do: Log in with a company business account, verify email and accept the Developer Terms of Service under My apps
Connect app: complete the request form (name without the word Pinterest, use case, privacy policy link) and submit for Trial
After approval, copy app ID and secret; add redirect URIs under Manage -> Configure -> Redirect URIs (exact match)
Implement OAuth with Basic-auth token exchange; refresh before 60 days; use the sandbox for test calls
Record a demo video showing the OAuth flow and one API action (Postman or terminal is accepted)
My apps -> Upgrade on the app card: verify details, upload the video, submit; watch email

roles.team: A Pinterest business account administers the app, with a verified email and accepted Developer Terms of Service under My apps. Use a company-owned business account.
roles.console: none documented in the pages read.
roles.customer: The Pinterest account owner who authorizes in the OAuth dialog; for ads:read, access to the relevant ad account is likely required.

testing: After Trial approval you get product-limited test tokens (24-hour expiry) and a Sandbox that does not affect production.
Trial output is visible only to its creator.

blockers.problem: Trial denial for an inaccessible privacy policy or vague app description
blockers.fix: Publish a working policy and a specific use case.

blockers.problem: Standard denial when the demo does not show authentication, uses non-OAuth methods like credentials or cookies, or lacks a live Pinterest integration
Trial-created Pins are visible only to the creator
blockers.fix: Production behavior cannot be validated until Standard.

blockers.problem: Refresh tokens expire after 60 days unused
blockers.fix: Refresh regularly or users must re-authorize.

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth and refresh code, draft the use-case and privacy-policy text, script the demo flow, run sandbox test calls.
automation.humanMust: Sign in and accept developer terms, submit the Trial and Upgrade requests, record the demo video, handle appeals through the Help Center.

uncertain: Exact review durations are not published beyond 'a few days'; scope list and per-scope requirements were not read in full; PKCE not mentioned.
